findings.message: All deterministic gates report success for this revision: bim_json_validation, gate_summary_binding (candidate/expected-facts/gate hashes consistent, issues empty), ifc_compile_reopen, geometry_success with zero issues, ifc_verification (no input or IFC issues), repair_route_terminal and semantic_coverage. Audit does not override these machine results and treats them as authoritative for this revision.

Supplied geometry metrics match the Design Brief without contradiction: floor slabs span x 0-24 / y 0-18 at z -0.2-0.0 and 3.4-3.6 m; roof slab at z 7.0-7.2 m as IfcSlab (PredefinedType ROOF, single slab, no IfcRoof container); light-court openings slab-storey-2-opening-light-court and roof-opening-light-court both resolve to x 8-16 / y 6-12, so the two openings are vertically aligned; stair opening slab-storey-2-opening-stair resolves to x 1-2.5 / y 5-11 and cuts the 200 mm slab; four railings sit at z 3.6-4.7 with 20 mm thickness and touch (not overlap) at the four court corners; storey wall tops meet slab undersides with no vertical gap (storey-1 walls 0-3.4, storey-2 walls 3.6-7.0).

All 15 door openings and 40 window openings have both an IfcRelVoidsElement against their host wall and an IfcRelFillsElement to a single IfcDoor or IfcWindow (recovered via text2ifc/filling-relationship-recovery/1.0). Each opening and its filling share the same local axis within the host wall frame: opening origins are expressed in the host wall's local X (wall length) axis, so openings on north-south walls span global X and openings on east-west partition/exterior walls span global Y; no case was found where an opening cuts across X while the filling spans along Y or the reverse. Sill/head placements are consistent with the brief (exterior double 600/3000, exterior single 1200/3000, interior double 900/3000).

Room-relative door swing direction is not geometrically expressed; only left/right handing is carried through the basic filling templates (IfcDoorStyle OperationType SINGLE_SWING_LEFT/RIGHT). This is an explicitly declared unsupported fact in the semantic capability profile (/known_facts/door/opening_direction) and is recorded in the candidate provenance as unverified, so it is a stated limitation rather than a silent semantic omission.

The inclined stair handrail is intentionally not modeled, as instructed by the user. The limitation is carried in the Design Brief stair limitations and repeated in the candidate provenance (engineering_unverified), so no fictitious handrail or post detail was introduced.

The three horizontal slabs carry material layer usage offset_from_reference_line = -200 with a total layer thickness of 200 mm (180 concrete + 20 mortar). This value is copied verbatim from the frozen Design Brief semantic requirements and is explicitly flagged in the candidate provenance as engineering-unverified relative to the slab placement origin convention. It is left as a non-blocking engineering-open item; it is not a user-fact contradiction and the deterministic geometry gate reports no slab issue.

Semantic coverage reports no blocking facts: all brief facts (building outline, storeys, walls, spaces, doors, windows, slabs, roof, stairs, railings, types, appearance, material, template) are marked represented, and the user constraints (no cross-storey light-court space, no full-height court wall or glass curtain, no extra beams/canopy/furniture, no performance properties, project-local types only, separate double-panel window widths not sharing one type) are honored in the terminal document. This support note does not by itself certify constructability or full code compliance.
